title_en: Krishnadas Is Shown the Path of Devotion
translation:
_Agalod gaamthi Krishnadas aavya, bhakti mukti paami haide harakhaya ||1||_ (Krishnadas came from the village of Agalod; having attained devotion and liberation, his heart rejoiced.)

Krishnadas's mother's name was Tejbai and his father's name was Damodardas Dave. In Idar, Damodardas Dave was a well-known physician (vaidya) and astrologer. Krishnadas was born in Samvat 1700, on the second day of the bright half of Kartak. In Samvat 1710, Damodardas passed away (attained the heavenly abode). In Samvat 1412, when the Muslims conquered Idar, Krishnadas, together with his mother, lived in Hidovar and pursued his studies there. He used to perform intense meditation (mahadhyan) on Ganpati. When Ganpati told him to ask for a boon, he asked instead for devotion to Shri Hari. Ganpati told him that only a Sadguru can grant the gift of devotion — devotion becomes firm through the company of saints (satsang). Ganpati then brought him, in the Kanam region, to Puniyad, to Sadguru Jivanji Maharaj, who was in the form of Sarangpani. At the edge of the village of Puniyad, a conversation took place with Naranadas. His doubts were resolved right there, and when he asked Naranadas for initiation (diksha), Naranadas brought him to Sadguru Jivanji Maharaj. Removing Krishnadas's doubt and confusion, Sadguru Jivanji Maharaj gave him initiation, gave him his own rosary (mala), and told him to give up the ritualistic worship of Omkar and to walk the path of [unclear] exclusive devotion (ananya bhakti) of the saints and devotees. Returning home from Puniyad to his native place, he came to Agalod, to the house of his host, the Kadva Kanbi Patel named Dhana.
